hints.title: Circle Tangent Pair Geometric Principle
hints.text: The optimal disk containing the maximum points can always be shifted until it has at least two points lying on its boundary.

hints.title: Center Determination from Point Pairs
hints.text: For each pair of darts with distance <= 2*r, calculate the midpoint and perpendicular bisector offset to locate both possible center circles.

hints.title: Point Distance Counting
hints.text: For each candidate center, count how many darts satisfy (x - cx)^2 + (y - cy)^2 <= r^2 + 1e-7.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import math

class Solution:
    def numPoints(self, darts: list[list[int]], r: int) -> int:
        n = len(darts)
        ans = 1
        for i in range(n):
            x1, y1 = darts[i]
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                x2, y2 = darts[j]
                d2 = (x1 - x2)**2 + (y1 - y2)**2
                if d2 > 4 * r * r:
                    continue
                d = math.sqrt(d2)
                mid_x, mid_y = (x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2
                h = math.sqrt(max(0.0, r * r - (d / 2)**2))
                vx, vy = -(y2 - y1) / d, (x2 - x1) / d
                for sign in [-1, 1]:
                    cx = mid_x + sign * h * vx
                    cy = mid_y + sign * h * vy
                    cnt = sum(1 for px, py in darts if (px - cx)**2 + (py - cy)**2 <= r * r + 1e-7)
                    if cnt > ans:
                        ans = cnt
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Testing all O(N^2) pairs against N darts runs in O(N^3) time, which takes milliseconds for N <= 100.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Continuous optimization over real coordinates cannot guarantee finding the global discrete maximum.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constraining search to pairwise boundary circles reduces continuous 2D geometry to finite candidates.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Understanding that any maximal circle touches at least 2 points and finding centers via perpendicular bisectors.
